content5.ptxt: The engine control computer monitors the purification condition of the catalyst using the 2 sensors installed upstream and downstream of the three-way catalytic converter. The air fuel ratio sensor sends a signal for the air-fuel ratio upstream of the catalyst to the engine control computer. The oxygen sensor sends a signal for the oxygen concentration downstream of the catalyst to the engine control computer. Based on the output voltage of the oxygen sensor, the engine control computer calculates the oxygen storage capacity (hereafter OSC) and detects catalyst deterioration.

While the vehicle is being driven after the engine has warmed up, the engine control computer performs active air-fuel ratio control for approximately 30 seconds or more. At this time, the engine control computer forcibly adjusts the air-fuel ratio to a lean or rich condition. If the lean/rich cycle of the oxygen sensor is long at this point, the OSC is judged to be large.
If the OSC value is equal to or less than the judgment value, the engine control computer determines that the catalyst has deteriorated and illuminates the check engine warning light.

entry.ptxt: When all of the following conditions are met

item.ptxt: Engine coolant temperature is 75°C or higher
Intake air temperature is -10°C or higher
Throttle valve is not fully closed
Air-fuel ratio feedback control in progress

entry.ptxt: Catalyst OSC value is equal to or less than judgment value
Detected 1 times during 1 trips (no detection after judgment)

topic.title: Confirmation Driving
topic.ptxt: By performing confirmation driving, it is possible to check whether the DTC is reproduced.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) display screen, switch from normal mode to check mode.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes.
Drive the vehicle at 75 to 80km/h for approximately 2 minutes (do not stop the engine during this time).
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the DTC result. (see )
The malfunction cannot be confirmed unless the test is performed properly.
Even if the vehicle stops during this confirmation test, it can be resumed without any problem.

atten4.ptxt: If there is a malfunction, the check engine warning light will illuminate during 7.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON. (C)
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes. (D)
Maintain the engine speed at 2500 - 3000r/min for approximately 3 minutes. (E)
Then maintain the engine speed at 3000r/min for 2 seconds, followed by 2000r/min for 2 seconds. (F)
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the output waveforms of [ECU Data Monitor] - [O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2] and [A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1].
If the output voltage of the air fuel ratio sensor or oxygen sensor does not fluctuate or has noise, the sensor may be malfunctioning.
If the output voltages of both sensors remain lean or rich, the air-fuel ratio may be extremely lean or rich.
When the catalyst deteriorates, the output voltage of the oxygen sensor changes greatly even under normal driving conditions.

atten4.ptxt: The malfunctioning area can be identified by performing the "Injection Volume" active test. This active test can decrease the fuel injection volume by -12.5 % or increase it by 25 %.

item.ptxt: Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes.
While depressing the accelerator pedal 60 % or more, keep the engine speed at 2500r/min for approximately 3 minutes to warm up each sensor.
Run the engine at idle, and read the output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor when the fuel injection volume is increased and decreased using the "Injection Volume" active test.

specitem.ptxt: The output voltages of the air fuel ratio sensor and oxygen sensor change according to the increase and decrease in fuel injection volume.

testgrp.testtitle: Read TaSCAN Data (A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1, A/F Sensor Voltage B2S1)

test1.ptxt: Connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3.
Turn IG ON.
Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes.
Depress the accelerator pedal and maintain 2500r/min for approximately 3 minutes to warm up the air fuel ratio sensor.
Allow the engine to idle.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, read [ECU Data Monitor] - [A/F Sensor Voltage B1S1 / A/F Sensor Voltage B2S1] and check that the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage is normal.

atten3.ptxt: Perform this immediately after warming up the sensor, as the air fuel ratio sensor will cool down.

test1.ptxt: Accelerate to 60 km/h and check that the output voltage of the air fuel ratio sensor rises (lean condition) when the accelerator pedal is released (during deceleration fuel cut).

item.ptxt: If the air fuel ratio sensor output is fixed at 3.3 V, the circuit may be open.
If the air fuel ratio sensor output is fixed at 3.8 V or more or 2.8 V or less, the circuit may be shorted.
When the engine control computer performs deceleration fuel cut, the air-fuel ratio becomes lean and the air fuel ratio sensor voltage rises.

The engine control computer needs to learn the throttle position fully closed position for fuel cut. If the battery terminal has been disconnected, the learned values are cancelled, so it is necessary to drive at 16 km/h or more to perform learning.
During acceleration, etc., the engine control computer temporarily increases the fuel amount, so the air fuel ratio sensor output voltage may be 2.8 V or less.

The air fuel ratio sensor uses a current detection element, so there is no voltage change even if the engine control computer terminal voltage is measured. The voltage displayed on SST (TaSCAN) is the current output by the air fuel ratio sensor converted into voltage.

testgrp.testtitle: Read TaSCAN Data (O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2, O2 Sensor Voltage B2S2)

test1.ptxt: Connect SST (TaSCAN) to DLC3.
Turn IG ON.
Turn the main switch of SST (TaSCAN) ON.
Start the engine, turn all accessory switches OFF, and warm up the engine until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes.
Depress the accelerator pedal and maintain 2500r/min for approximately 3 minutes to warm up the oxygen sensor.
Race the engine several times at an engine speed of 4000r/min.
Allow the engine to idle.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, read the oxygen sensor voltage waveform displayed in [ECU Data Monitor] - [O2 Sensor Voltage B1S2 / O2 Sensor Voltage B2S2].

specitem.ptxt: A voltage of 0.4V or less and 0.5V or more is output.

atten3.ptxt: Perform this immediately after warming up the sensor, as the oxygen sensor will cool down.
